memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The tribe of Benjamin, according to its clans, had the following towns: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz, Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Kephar Ammoni, Ophni and Geba—twelve towns and their villages - Josh 18:21-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the towns of Benjamin are listed — twelve of them, each a real place where families would settle. Among them is Jericho, the very city whose walls had fallen at the start of the conquest, and Bethel, the house of God. The list joins together places of great memory and ordinary villages alike, all now part of the settled inheritance of God's people.

It is worth pausing on Jericho appearing here. The city that had been a fortress of opposition, whose walls God brought down, is now simply one of Benjamin's towns — a place of homes and daily life. What was once a stronghold of the enemy has become part of God's people's inheritance. The place of battle has become a place of belonging. God turns former battlegrounds into settled homes.

This is a hopeful pattern to notice. The very places in our lives that were once sites of struggle and opposition can, by God's grace, become places of peace and dwelling. Jericho the fortress becomes Jericho the hometown. God does not merely bring us through our battles; He can transform the ground of those battles into settled, fruitful territory. The stronghold that once loomed over us can become, in time, a place where we quietly live in God's provision. He redeems even our hardest ground.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What former "Jericho" — a place of struggle — might God be turning into settled ground?
- Do you believe God can transform your battlegrounds into places of peace?
- How does God's redemption of hard ground give you hope today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You turn former battlegrounds into settled homes. Where I have known struggle, bring Your peace, and make even my hardest ground a place of Your provision. Amen.
